CHIEF COMPLAINT
Back pain and tingling in right foot.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports onset of back tightening and pins and needles sensation in right foot approximately two hours after raking leaves in yard yesterday. Patient had similar back pain episode approximately three years ago that resolved after one day. Patient attempted treatment with ice and two doses of ibuprofen without relief. Pain worsens with bending over, improves with hot shower and sitting. Pain with palpation noted around L5. Partner reports pain is worse when patient stands up. Patient reports high pain tolerance and states this is concerning. On physical examination, dorsiflexion is normal, pulses equal in all extremities, tingling sensation in right leg confirmed. X-ray of low back shows normal findings.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for back pain and tingling in right leg. Negative for pain on spinal extension.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Prior episode of back pain approximately three years ago that resolved spontaneously.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports normally does not engage in physical activity. Patient was raking leaves at time of injury onset.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Low back: Pain with flexion, pain with palpation at L5, no pain with extension. Lower extremities: Dorsiflexion normal bilaterally, pulses equal in all extremities. Neurologic: Tingling sensation in right leg.

RESULTS
X-ray of low back: Normal.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Low back strain. Plan includes: Rest, prescribe meloxicam, prescribe physical therapy to include stretches and exercises to improve conditioning. Patient to contact provider in two weeks if pain not improving, at which time MRI will be considered if symptoms persist.
